prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a low-speed head-on collision in Conroe, Texas, and has concussion. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1358; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement concerns the collision you were involved in on the roadway in Conroe, Texas. Please state your full name for the record.

A: Sure. I'd rather not put my name on a recording just yet, if that's okay. I can still answer your questions.

Q: That's fine. For the record, can you describe what you were doing just before the collision?

A: I was driving home from work, heading down the two-lane road. It was a normal drive, maybe a little after the afternoon rush.

Q: How fast were you traveling?

A: I'd guess around thirty-five miles an hour. I wasn't in any hurry.

Q: Can you tell me what happened when the other vehicle came toward you?

A: The other car crossed into my lane. I hit the brakes and turned, but we still ended up meeting nose to nose. It didn't feel like a big impact, more like a hard jolt.

Q: Did your airbags deploy?

A: Yes, they did. My head snapped back and then forward. I felt dazed for a minute.

Q: Did you seek medical attention afterward?

A: I went to the emergency room that evening. They diagnosed me with a concussion and told me to rest and avoid screens for a while.

Q: Are you still experiencing symptoms?

A: Yes. I get headaches, I'm sensitive to light, and I've had trouble concentrating at work. My doctor said recovery could take a few more weeks.

Q: Thank you. Is there anything you would like to add to your statement?

A: Only that I'm cooperating fully and I hope this gets sorted out soon.

Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
